title: Shard Mode and Median Reducer
prompt:
Implement `reduce_shard_statistics(shards) -> tuple[int, float]`. `shards` is an iterable of finite iterables of integer observations. Treat all observations across every shard as one multiset and return `(mode, median)`. The mode is the value with the highest global frequency; if several values tie, return the smallest such value. The median is the middle value for an odd number of observations, or the arithmetic mean of the two middle values for an even number, always returned as a `float`.

Use space proportional to the number of distinct values rather than materializing all observations. Empty shards are valid, but raise an error when there are no observations in total. Every observation must be an `int`; otherwise raise an error. Do not mutate a caller-owned shard.

Invalid inputs may be rejected with `assert`.

example.reasoning: Values 1 and 3 each appear twice, so the tie rule selects 1; the two middle sorted values are 2 and 3.
